verdict.rationale: The evidence shows no first-party feature in Stripe Issuing for creating background automations, such as scheduled jobs or user-configurable workflow rules. What it does show are adjacent pieces: spending controls that are enforced automatically, a synchronous authorization webhook a developer must build against, and virtual cards that external agents use to buy things on their own. In those cases the autonomy belongs to the developer's code or the agent, not to an automation capability of Issuing itself, so none of them earns credit.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background
